+export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(

+  isHost: boolean
+): boolean {
+  const requirement = setting ?? RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;
+
+  switch (requirement) {
+    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
+      return false;
+    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
+      return true;
+    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
+      return isHost;
+    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
+      return !isHost;
+    default:
+      return false;
+  }
+}

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 18:49:04Z)**_

I found the actual root cause, and it's more significant than a test-fixture gap — it's a real production bug. Before I touch anything, let me explain and confirm the approach, since it involves a schema/migration change (which your CLAUDE.md explicitly flags as "ask first").

**The bug:** `packages/prisma/migrations/20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql` adds the column with `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`:
```sql
ALTER TABLE "public"."EventType" ADD COLUMN "requiresRescheduleReason" "public"."RescheduleReasonRequirement" DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```
In Postgres, `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT X` backfills **every existing row**, not just new ones. That means every pre-existing event type on any Cal.diy install — never opted into this feature — would suddenly require hosts to enter a reason on every reschedule after this migration runs. That's an unannounced breaking behavior change, and it's exactly why `handleSeats.test.ts` and `webhook-producer-booking-requested.test.ts` broke: their event-type fixtures don't set the new field, so they inherit "mandatory" instead of the old no-requirement behavior.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 18:52:19Z)**_

- **Change default to OPTIONAL_BOTH (Recommended)** - Update schema.prisma default, the migration.sql DEFAULT value, and the isRescheduleReasonRequired() fallback so unconfigured event types behave as before (no reason required) until a host explicitly turns the setting on. Fixes both the production breaking-change bug and the 4 failing tests.
- **Only patch the two failing test files** - Leave MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY as the default and just update handleSeats.test.ts / webhook-producer-booking-requested.test.ts fixtures to set requiresRescheduleReason: OPTIONAL_BOTH (or pass a reason). Makes tests pass but leaves the breaking-change behavior in production for every existing event type.


**Answer:** Change default to OPTIONAL_BOTH (Recommended)

995	  updatedAt       DateTime?   @updatedAt
996	  // Used to identify a watched calendar channel in Google Calendar
997	  // @deprecated use channelId instead
998	  googleChannelId String?
999	
1000	  // @deprecated use channelKind instead
1001	  googleChannelKind String?
1002	
1003	  // @deprecated use channelResourceId instead
1004	  googleChannelResourceId String?
1005	
1006	  // @deprecated use channelResourceUri instead
1007	  googleChannelResourceUri String?
1008	
1009	  // @deprecated use channelExpoiration instead
1010	  googleChannelExpiration String?
1011	
1012	  // Used to identify a watched calendar
1013	  channelId          String?
1014	  channelKind        String?
1015	  channelResourceId  String?
1016	  channelResourceUri String?
1017	  channelExpiration  DateTime? @db.Timestamp(3)
1018	
1019	  // Used to calendar cache and sync
1020	  syncSubscribedAt         DateTime? @db.Timestamp(3)
1021	  syncSubscribedErrorAt    DateTime? @db.Timestamp(3)
1022	  syncSubscribedErrorCount Int       @default(0)
1023	  syncToken                String?

1028	  delegationCredential   DelegationCredential? @relation(fields: [delegationCredentialId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
1029	  delegationCredentialId String?

1031	  error           String?

1033	  watchAttempts   Int       @default(0)
1034	  unwatchAttempts Int       @default(0)
1035	  maxAttempts     Int       @default(3)
1036	
1037	  eventTypeId Int?
1038	  eventType   EventType? @relation(fields: [eventTypeId], references: [id])
1039	
1040	  calendarCacheEvents CalendarCacheEvent[]
1041	
1042	  // It could still allow multiple user-level(eventTypeId is null) selected calendars for same userId, integration, externalId because NULL is not equal to NULL
1043	  // We currently ensure uniqueness by checking for the existence of the record before creating a new one
1044	  // Think about introducing a generated unique key ${userId}_${integration}_${externalId}_${eventTypeId}
1045	  @@unique([userId, integration, externalId, eventTypeId])
1046	  @@unique([googleChannelId, eventTypeId])

1048	  @@index([externalId])
1049	  @@index([eventTypeId])
1050	  @@index([credentialId])
1051	  @@index([channelId])
1052	  // Composite indices to optimize calendar-cache queries
1053	  @@index([integration, googleChannelExpiration, error, watchAttempts, maxAttempts], name: "SelectedCalendar_watch_idx")
1054	  @@index([integration, googleChannelExpiration, error, unwatchAttempts, maxAttempts], name: "SelectedCalendar_unwatch_idx")
1055	}

**Root cause:** `packages/prisma/migrations/20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql` added the new column with `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`, which Postgres backfills onto every existing row — silently requiring a reschedule reason from hosts on every pre-existing event type, and breaking pre-existing seat-reschedule/webhook-producer tests that predate this feature.

**Fix (5 files, 23+/14-):**
- `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` + the migration SQL: default changed to `OPTIONAL_BOTH`
- `packages/features/bookings/lib/rescheduleReason.ts`: fallback for an unset setting changed from `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` to `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, with a comment explaining why
- `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx`: matching UI default fix (was pre-selecting "Mandatory for host only" for unconfigured event types, which would have silently opted them in on save)
- `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/test/reschedule.test.ts`: updated the one test that explicitly asserted the old (buggy) default behavior

**Verified:**
- The 4 previously-broken tests (`handleSeats.test.ts` ×3, `webhook-producer-booking-requested.test.ts` ×1) now pass, plus both Issue #11 tests and the analogous `handleCancelBooking.test.ts` (to confirm the sibling cancellation-reason feature is untouched) — 85 passed, 1 todo, 0 failed across all 5 files.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/web` (covers `packages/features`) passes clean, 0 errors. (`yarn type-check:ci` itself is broken by a pre-existing Windows environment issue — `spawn tsc ENOENT` — unrelated to this change; every non-trivial package fails identically.)

**One important incident during investigation, now resolved:** `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` (2,859 lines) was silently truncated to 0 bytes on disk sometime during my worktree-based test runs — not something I intentionally touched, most likely a build/postinstall script that resolved a path back to your main working directory instead of the isolated worktree. I caught it via a full-tree scan, restored it byte-for-byte from git before making any further edits, and swept the rest of the tree for similar damage (found none besides the harmless `sprite.svg` line-ending diff). Worth mentioning to your team if you use worktrees elsewhere in this repo.

I have not committed or pushed anything — this is all still uncommitted in your working tree, ready for you to review and commit when you're satisfied.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 19:23:02Z)**_

That confirms it. Here's the full picture of your 19 remaining failures:

**Root cause: `packages/prisma/.env` was a git-tracked symlink that Windows couldn't materialize** (needs Developer Mode/symlink privileges, which this environment lacks). It showed as "deleted" in `git status`, and something in the calendar-subscription service's import chain reads env vars from that specific path at module-load time — when it's missing, vitest's automocking of `CalendarSyncService` silently produces a broken (non-constructor) mock, cascading into 17 failing tests across both calendar-subscription route test files.

I copied your root `.env` into `packages/prisma/.env` as a plain file (not a symlink) to work around the Windows privilege issue, and re-ran the previously-failing tests:

| Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|
| 19 failed | **2 failed** |
| 17 calendar-subscription tests | 0 |
| `next-config.test.ts` | still fails (pre-existing) |
| `pagesAndRewritePaths.test.ts` | still fails (pre-existing) |

Those last 2 are the same failures I found on `team/main` and on the commit immediately before your 3 Issue #11 commits — confirmed unrelated to your change, and unrelated to this `.env` issue too (they're their own separate pre-existing environment/config quirk).

**None of this was caused by my reschedule-reason fix** — the calendar-subscription failures are a local dev-environment gap, not a code regression.

⚠️ **One important thing before you commit anything:** `packages/prisma/.env` is now a real file containing your actual secrets (DATABASE_URL, etc.), not a symlink. Git sees it as a "typechange." **Do not `git add -A` or otherwise stage this file** — it should stay untracked/ignored locally. If you want a permanent fix instead of this workaround, enable Windows Developer Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security → For developers) so git can create real symlinks, then this file will resolve correctly on its own.

Your full suite should now show just those 2 known pre-existing failures plus whatever normal flakiness exists — nothing tied to Issue #11.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 19:37:49Z)**_

Found it — and it's a real, separate, pre-existing issue. I need to correct my earlier claim.

**What's actually going on:** the calendar-subscription tests are **genuinely flaky at the full-suite scale**, independent of the `.env` fix. Look at the actual error:

```
EnvironmentTeardownError: Cannot load '.../encodeOAuthState.ts' imported from
.../office365video/api/add.ts after the environment was torn down.
```

The app-store's generated service maps (`calendar.services.generated.ts`, `video.adapters.generated.ts` — both already in your dirty file list) use dynamic `import()` calls keyed by provider name. Under vitest's parallel/threaded test execution, one of those dynamic imports can resolve *after* the test environment that triggered it has already been torn down (because a different, unrelated test finished first). When that race hits, it corrupts whatever calendar-subscription test happens to be running at that moment — which is why the exact failure count is non-deterministic:
- My earlier isolated 4-file run: 0 calendar-subscription failures (no other tests to race against)
- First full-suite re-run just now: 11 failures (cron file clean, only webhook file hit)
- Second, `apps/web`-only run: 19 failures (both files hit)

This is a pre-existing vitest/test-infrastructure race condition, unrelated to Issue #11 and unrelated to my `.env` fix or the reschedule-reason fix — it would flake the same way on `team/main` or any other branch if run enough times under load. I was wrong to tell you it "should now show just 2" — that was based on a small run that didn't have enough concurrent tests to trigger the race.

**What I can confirm cleanly:** none of this touches reschedule/booking code. Want me to run the suite once with `--no-file-parallelism` (single-threaded, so no races possible) to get you a fully deterministic count for the PR? It'll be much slower (probably 15-20+ min for 4,146 tests) but will show only genuinely code-caused failures.

commit facbda2a9a33afa2c1fb73ff40b1b258b7ca62cf
Author: Julissa Hernandez <jehernandezper@wm.edu>
Date:   Thu Sep 17 16:46:22 2026 -0400

    fix(bookings): default reschedule reason requirement to optional
    
    The migration for requiresRescheduleReason defaulted unset event types
    to MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY, which is a breaking change: Postgres backfills
    ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT onto every existing row, so all pre-existing
    event types would have started requiring a host reschedule reason.
    It also broke handleSeats.test.ts and webhook-producer-booking-requested.test.ts,
    whose fixtures predate this feature and don't supply a reason.
    
    Default unset event types to OPTIONAL_BOTH (no requirement) instead,
    matching non-breaking-change conventions, and align the EventAdvancedTab
    UI default and the reschedule.test.ts expectation accordingly.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

=== rescheduleReason.ts on PR #36 tip ===
import { RescheduleReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(
  setting: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

Yes — each git worktree is a completely separate physical directory with its own `node_modules` folder (this repo uses Yarn's `node-modules` linker, not a shared cache-only mode), so each one needs its own `yarn install` before I can run tests in it.

The good news: it's fast, because I point `YARN_CACHE_FOLDER` at your main repo's existing `.yarn/cache`, so it reuses already-downloaded packages instead of re-downloading anything from the network — it just needs to link them into that worktree's own `node_modules`. This is the same approach I used for the earlier investigation worktrees (`team/main`, pre-Issue-11, etc.), and none of it touches your actual working directory at `C:\Users\Julissa\CSCI 435Project\cal.diy` — it's all in a disposable folder at `C:\wt-v2` that I'll clean up when we're done.

---rescheduleReason.ts---
import { RescheduleReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(
  setting: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case RescheduleReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 21:27:02Z)**_

Same fix as before — reapplying it here as part of step 1 since we're rebuilding cleanly.

**The bug:** the cherry-picked commit (`35d7f6c3bd`) added a `requiresRescheduleReason` column with `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`. In Postgres, `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT X` backfills that value onto **every existing row**, not just new ones — so every pre-existing event type (which never opted into this feature) would silently start requiring hosts to enter a reason when rescheduling. It also broke two pre-existing tests (`handleSeats.test.ts`, `webhook-producer-booking-requested.test.ts`) that predate this feature and don't supply a reason.

**The fix (4 edits, just applied):**
1. `schema.prisma` — default changed from `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` → `OPTIONAL_BOTH`
2. `migration.sql` — same default change
3. `rescheduleReason.ts` — the fallback for an unset/null setting changed to `OPTIONAL_BOTH` instead of `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`
4. `reschedule.test.ts` — updated the one test that explicitly asserted the old buggy behavior ("unset defaults to mandatory") to instead expect the corrected behavior ("unset defaults to no requirement")

Net effect: rescheduling only requires a reason when someone explicitly turns that setting on for a specific event type — not automatically for everyone. I'll show you the test results for this step as soon as they finish.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 21:35:41Z)**_

Good news — it's currently **unstaged**, not staged (git shows it under "Changes not staged for commit"). If your IDE's source control panel shows it in a "staged" section, that might just be how that tool categorizes typechanges, or you may have clicked to stage it there — worth double-checking in your tool.

**What "typechange" means:** git tracks `packages/prisma/.env` in this repo as a **symlink** (mode `120000`, pointing to `../../.env`, confirmed via `git ls-files -s`). On this Windows machine, git can't create real symlinks without Developer Mode enabled, so when I copied your root `.env` content into that path as a workaround (so Prisma-dependent tests could find it), it became a **plain regular file** instead of a symlink. Git sees "the type of filesystem object at this path changed" (symlink → regular file) — that's what `T` / "typechange" means, as opposed to `M` (content changed) or `D`/`A` (deleted/added).

**Why this matters — please don't stage or commit it:** this file now contains a literal copy of your real `.env` secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, etc.), not a symlink reference. If it ever gets committed, those secrets would be pushed to the repo. Leave it unstaged; it's just a local workaround so tests can run, not something that belongs in any commit.

**Permanent fix (optional):** enable Windows Developer Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security → For developers), then git can create the actual symlink and this typechange will stop appearing entirely.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Event types can already force a **cancellation** reason. The `CancellationReasonRequirement` enum (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`) offers `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` / `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, it is stored on `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:287`), and it is enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`.

Rescheduling has no equivalent. A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`, `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but it is always optional — `rg -n "requiresRescheduleReason|RescheduleReasonRequirement"` over the repo returns nothing.

So a host who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, even though a reschedule disrupts the same attendee and moves the same calendar. Hosts who run paid or high-demand event types are the ones who feel it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Mirror the cancellation setting for reschedules:

- a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a `requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, with the same four values and the same default posture;
- a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced, sitting next to the cancellation one;
- validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`;
- the reason surfaced wherever the cancellation reason already is.

### User story

As a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.

### Rough scope

**Medium.** The whole pattern already exists end to end — enum, column, migration (`packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/`), settings dropdown, validation, and unit tests in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts` — so this is one migration plus a parallel copy of known-good code, not a new design.

### Source

`specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/future-work.md`, which lists "Reschedule reason requirement (same pattern, separate setting)" as work deliberately deferred from that feature.

### Additional context

Intended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: medium`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.
